text:
J.T. Miller, the Rangers' captain, had a rough week in the headlines. The New York Post reported he was dropped from the top power-play unit as Mike Sullivan hunts for answers, and four goals in 17 games won't quiet anyone. Look at even strength, though, and he might be the best thing the Rangers have going.

At 5v5 New York gets 63% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Miller on the ice, about 17 points better than without him. That's dominant. The goals just haven't come: four on 6.3 expected for him, and his teammates have scored 6.3 fewer than their chances with him out there. Both usually swing back. Evolving-Hockey told the same story about last season, when his chances were worth far more than his results. Our hunch is the power-play demotion matters less than it sounds, because the scoring he's missing is the 5v5 kind, and that's where he's driving the play. When the bounces turn, his point total will catch up with how well he's played.
headline: Miller is driving play; the goals are late
